items.title: Full-Body, Hand & Facial Motion Capture From Any Video In Blender
items.excerpt: BlendCap, a new Blender add-on from Arcomade, tracks full-body, hand, and facial motion from a single recorded video and retargets the performance onto game rigs (Rigify, Auto-Rig Pro, Mixamo, CloudRig) locally, with no internet required. It brings markerless video-to-motion capture — an ML pose-estimation capability that once needed suits and studios — directly into the game-character animation pipeline.

items.title: Reddit is forcing Google AI into hallucinating The Duskbloods characters before FromSoftware's game is even out
items.excerpt: Fans have spent months inventing fake lore and bosses for FromSoftware's unreleased The Duskbloods on Reddit, and Google's AI Overviews are now surfacing those fabrications as fact. It's a vivid example of generative AI confidently hallucinating game content from unreliable community sources — a growing headache for studios trying to control the narrative and information around unreleased titles.

items.title: Good games will get cloned and buried: AI vibe coding is one of the biggest threats on storefronts like Steam, analyst warns
items.excerpt: An industry analyst warns that AI 'vibe coding' is one of the biggest threats on storefronts like Steam, cautioning that well-made games risk being cloned and buried under a flood of quickly AI-generated titles. A look at how low-friction, prompt-driven game-making is reshaping the economics and discoverability of the market.

items.title: Half of all games released on Steam will use AI by 2028, study predicts: 'AI lowers the barrier not just to make a game but to make several'
items.excerpt: A study predicts AI-flagged titles will cross roughly half of all new Steam releases around 2027-2028, arguing generative AI 'lowers the barrier not just to make a game but to make several.' A signal of how AI is reshaping game creation velocity and storefront discoverability.
